first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. The most recent validated learnings show that both signup simplification (memory_31) and onboarding shortening (memory_86) durably improved early engagement metrics. These are directly applicable to the current activation decline. Verifying these two memories will confirm the magnitude of past lift and any retention/cohort quality caveats before running a new test. Simplify_onboarding is preferable to promotional_pricing because: (1) pricing pressure from competitors typically creates races-to-the-bottom that harm long-term revenue (memory_73 showed retention damage); (2) onboarding friction is a root cause we can address without margin erosion; (3) activation_messaging alone is lower-impact than structural onboarding changes; (4) enterprise_sales_assist requires sales ops setup and doesn't address the self-serve SMB majority being lost to competitor pricing. A small guarded test preserves optionality if results prove underwhelming.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both signup simplification and onboarding shortening are durable levers with positive retention profiles (exp_86 showed +3% 30-day retention; exp_31 showed only -1% with strong revenue lift). Current activation and completion declines are directly addressable by these mechanisms. Escalating to standard_experiment rather than small_guarded_test because: (1) two independent sources show +13% and +9% activation/completion lifts with minimal retention risk; (2) the activation decline is material (6% QoQ) and we have strong historical validation; (3) we have one experiment slot this week and cannot afford high caution when the evidence base is this solid. Enterprise_sales_assist and promotional_pricing remain suboptimal—the former doesn't scale to the SMB activation problem, the latter creates margin and retention damage per memory_73. This move directly counters the competitor threat by improving product engagement, not by racing on price.
